## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One Important defect needs fixing. When `--json` comes before another flag and has no path, `parse_args` takes the next flag as the JSON path. So the "default destination … alongside the required --junit destination" case in the pull-request description fails for `--json --junit out.xml`. This review found no Critical defects in the two changed files, both of which were read in full.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/cli.py:15 — correctness — `parse_args(["--json", "--junit", "out.xml"])` raises `ValueError("unknown option: out.xml")` instead of returning `{"json": "results.json", "junit": "out.xml"}`. The `--json` branch only checks `i + 1 < len(args)`, so it takes `"--junit"` as the JSON path (line 16), skips past it (lines 18–19), and then treats `out.xml` as a flag. With `["--json", "--junit"]`, it instead returns `{"json": "--junit"}`, and `write_reports` would create a file named `--junit`. Apply the same `args[i + 1].startswith("--")` check that the `--junit` branch uses at line 7 before taking the next argument. Also add a test for `["--json", "--junit", "x.xml"]`: `tests/test_cli.py:43-47` only covers `--json` as the last argument. — Users who put `--json` before `--junit` without a path get a misleading "unknown option" error or a JSON report written to a file named after a flag. The comment at app/cli.py:12 ("JSON can use its default destination when no path is supplied") is true only when `--json` is the last argument.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- The `--junit` branch now takes its value as `args[i + 1]` before advancing the index, which is clearer than before. `tests/test_cli.py:50-55` covers its success case and both missing-path error paths (end of args, and followed by another flag).
- `write_reports` is tested by writing a real file under `tmp_path` and reading it back (`tests/test_cli.py:45-47`), rather than mocking `Path`.

(none)
